record.paper_title: Stellar model calibrations with the Ai Phe binary system. Open questions about the robustness of the fit
record.original_question: What is the relation, if any, between stellar mass and the convective core overshooting parameter β that measures the extent of extra mixing beyond the formal convective-core boundary in stellar evolution models? In particular, can a physically meaningful mass–β relation be established, or do different analyses of binary-star systems support incompatible values of β even when the stellar masses are well measured?

evidence.quote: Many authors have attempted to determine the exact relation, if any, between the stellar mass and the value of the convective core overshooting parameter, with opposing findings

artifact.self_contained_problem: In stellar evolution modeling, the boundary of a star's convective core is conventionally located where the Schwarzschild (or Ledoux) criterion is marginally satisfied. To account for inertial penetration of fluid elements beyond this formal boundary, one introduces a convective-core overshooting parameter β ≥ 0, which prescribes that the mixed region extends a distance β·H_p beyond the formal core edge, where H_p is the local pressure scale height (with appropriate modification for very small cores). The value of β controls the size of the mixed core during the main sequence and thus strongly influences a star's evolutionary track, lifetime, and observable properties.\n\nConsider main-sequence and post-main-sequence stars with masses M in a range (roughly 1.1 M_⊙ ≲ M ≲ 10 M_⊙) for which a convective core is present and overshooting is dynamically relevant. Determine whether there exists a well-defined, physically meaningful function β = β(M) (possibly depending also on metallicity and evolutionary phase) such that stellar evolution models using β(M) simultaneously reproduce the observed properties (masses, radii, effective temperatures, luminosities, and ages) of independent calibrators, in particular detached eclipsing binary systems with precisely measured component masses. Equivalently: prove or disprove that the calibrations of β derived from different binary systems (and from other observational constraints such as cluster isochrones and asteroseismology) at comparable stellar masses are mutually consistent, or exhibit them as incompatible and characterize the source of the discrepancy.
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple independent studies of detached eclipsing binaries, open clusters, and asteroseismic targets have proposed mass–β relations, but they disagree in both the functional form and the calibrated values of β at fixed mass. Recent works (Claret & Torres; Constantino & Baraffe; Tkachenko et al.; Higl et al.) report mutually inconsistent calibrations, and the issue remains an active and unresolved area of stellar astrophysics.

status_evidence.title: Claret & Torres 2019 — The dependence of convective core overshooting on stellar mass
status_evidence.snippet: We have continued our investigation aimed at calibrating the strength of convective core overshooting in stars... The semi-empirical mass-overshooting relation is reaffirmed.
status_evidence.claim: One line of work argues for a definite mass–β relation increasing with mass.

status_evidence.title: Constantino & Baraffe 2018 — Significance of the overshooting parameter calibrations
status_evidence.snippet: We find that the apparent mass-overshooting relation found by some authors is not statistically significant given the uncertainties on the data.
status_evidence.claim: A contrasting analysis finds no statistically significant mass–β relation, indicating the question remains contested.
